title: Trump’s Justice Dept. Targets Smaller Fraud Cases
summary: As the Trump administration drops charges against corporations and the wealthy, it is also taking aim at small-scale fraud cases, including against the operator of a weathered food truck in California.

title: Trump Gives Green Light to U.S. Companies to Aim Hacks at Cybercriminals
summary: The practice would align the United States more closely with countries like China and Russia, where spy agencies have long relied on private-sector hackers to help with national security missions.

title: Concerns Grow Over Conditions on Aircraft Carrier, and Trump Pushes New Hacking Effort
summary: Plus, your Friday news quiz.

title: U.S.S. Abraham Lincoln Has Been Deployed for Months, Prompting Concerns
summary: The U.S.S. Abraham Lincoln has been deployed for nearly nine months. Members of Congress are worried about the crew’s well-being.

title: What to Know About Luigi Mangione’s Court Cases and Potential Plea
summary: Mr. Mangione faces federal charges of stalking that resulted in the death of a health insurance executive. A guilty plea could close the federal case — and complicate a separate state murder trial.

title: Russia Campaigned to Derail Moldova’s Pro-Western Government
summary: In Moldova, Moscow paid Orthodox priests, conducted a vote-buying scheme and set up training camps on election interference — all in an effort to derail the Western-leaning government.

title: How Thrillers Hook You With Their First Sentence
summary: Can our Book Review editor, Tina Jordan, guess thrillers from their first sentence? In this game we explore a few of the books from The New York Times’s “50 Best Thrillers of the 21st Century” list; and learn a bit more about why opening sentences are so important to get people reading.

title: Readers Choose the Best Thrillers and Mysteries of the Century
summary: The backbone of the list: nine novels by Tana French, and five novels each from John le Carré, Kate Atkinson and Mick Herron.

title: Great Movie and TV Adaptations From 21st- Century Thrillers
summary: From “Slow Horses” to “Big Little Lies,” our list of great psychological thrillers, spy novels and crime fiction have inspired a heap of great adaptations.

title: Farage Wins Special U.K. Election That He Initiated, as Expected
summary: Nigel Farage, the leader of Reform U.K., won the Clacton by-election with 63 percent. Count Binface, a novelty candidate, came second with 27 percent, a personal best.

title: Deaths of 3 ICE Detainees Prompt Questions About Medical Care
summary: Immigrants at Delaney Hall in Newark have complained about health services. Federal officials defended the treatment provided there and elsewhere.

title: As Europe Gets Hotter, Its Transportation Systems Struggle to Cope
summary: The continent’s railways and roads “were engineered for a climate that no longer exists,” one expert said.

title: More Wildfires and Extreme Heat Roil Europe, but Relief Is on the Horizon
summary: Another day of near record heat baked the continent on Friday, but temperatures could retreat to seasonal averages in the coming days.

title: Chatbots Are Pushing Us Toward a Post-Human Internet
summary: In matters of work, school and even romance, we turn to A.I. chatbots. But what happens when the bots begin talking to one another?

title: Afghan Women Erased From Public Life in Five Years of Taliban Rule
summary: Decrees restricting the rights of women and girls to study, work, travel and act independently now threaten to damage Afghanistan permanently, experts say.

title: An Unlikely Emergency Appeal to the Supreme Court From a Dog Named Bruce
summary: A last-ditch filing this week came on behalf of a dog that a judge found to be “vicious” and shows how the court’s emergency docket has been growing.

title: Gone in 20 Minutes: Half-Off Sushi Draws Throngs to New York’s Japanese Markets
summary: At a proliferating number of stores, discounts on items like sushi are offered after 8 p.m. To get the best meals, you have to be there early.

title: Is Ocasio-Cortez Ready for the Glass Cliff?
summary: She will run as a woman but unlike how every woman before her was forced to run.

title: Extreme Heat Is the New Normal
summary: Firefighters in Phoenix race to save lives in a city that’s only getting hotter.

title: Are Political Polls Accurate?
summary: We look at recent problems with political polling.

title: Jimmy Fallon Reacts to Karoline Leavitt’s White House Exit
summary: The “Tonight Show” host said President Trump had been surprised by the press secretary’s decision to step down. “She was like, ‘I wanted to wait for a good time but there hasn’t been one, so.’”

title: Federal Job Cuts Are Making Wildfires Harder to Fight
summary: The Trump administration pushed out thousands of veteran U.S. Forest Service staff. An ‘extraordinary’ fire season is testing those who are left.
